title: Derivative condition at a quotient maximum
statement: Let $f,g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ and $x,r,a,b\in\mathbb{R}$. Suppose $f$ is differentiable at $x$ with derivative $a$, $g$ is differentiable at $x$ with derivative $b$, $g(x)=1$, and $t\mapsto f(t)/g(t)^r$ has a local maximum at $x$. Then $a=r f(x)b$.
hypotheses_covered: $t\mapsto f(t)/g(t)^r$ has a local maximum at $x$
replaced: Let $f,g:\bbr\to\bbr$ be differentiable at $x$, with $f^{\prime}(x)=a$, $g^{\prime}(x)=b$, and $g(x)=1$. If $t\mapsto f(t)/g(t)^r$ has a local maximum at $x$ for $r\in\bbr$, then $a=rf(x)b$.
